title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC mode-difference; gift vs imputation clash
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: GAR has now conceded the modes differ—Adam's disobedience does not constitute us sinners before the tribunal in just the same way Christ's obedience constitutes us righteous—so the likeness must not be pressed as if mode were identical; that was the whole point of the question, and the reply helps Placeus, not against him. But some things deserve censure. First, saying Christ's righteousness is ours only by imputation, while also holding Adam's sin ours only by imputation, erases mode-difference in that point and clashes with the Apostle, who hints a great difference by calling Christ's side gift, grace, and a donation of grace—the mode by which it becomes ours, a mode Adam's sin never had and could not have.
pass_b_english: PLAC. The learned man therefore acknowledges that we are not constituted sinners before God's tribunal by Adam's disobedience in altogether the same mode in which we are constituted righteous by Christ's obedience: and so that likeness is not to be pressed as if there were no difference in the mode: and this is the whole of what we meant to prove by this interrogation, if indeed we used it. Therefore his reply fights for us, not against us. Yet some things in it seem worthy of censure. First, that he says Christ's righteousness is ours only by imputation: for if likewise, as he everywhere contends, Adam's sin is ours only by imputation, both are ours in the same mode, and there is no difference in that point. That clashes with the Apostle, who hints a very great difference in the mode by which Christ's righteousness and Adam's unrighteousness are ours, when he calls the former a gift, and grace, and a donation which is of grace: for so he signifies the mode by which it becomes ours—a mode in which Adam's sin neither was made ours, nor could be.
source_text: PLAC. Agnoscit ergo vir doctus non eodem prorsus modo per Adami inobedientiam nos coram tribunali Dei constitui peccatores, quo per Christi obedientiam constituimur justi: itaque non esse urgandam illam similitudinem, quasi nullum esset in modo discrimen: hoc vero est totum, quod hac interrogatione, siquidem ea sumus usi, probare instituimus. Quare pro nobis, non contra nos haec eius militat responsio. Videntur tamen in ea quaedam digna reprehensione. Illud in primis, quod ait, justitiam Christi nostram non esse nisi imputatione: nam si similiter, ut passim contendit, peccatum Adami nostrum non est nisi imputatione, eodem modo ambo nostra sunt, nec ea in re ullum est discrimen. Id quod pugnat cum Apostolo, maximum in modo, quo nostra sunt, justitia Christi & iniustitia Adami, discrimen innuente, cum illam appellat donum, & gratiam, & donationem quae est ex gratia: sic enim modum significat quo fit nostra: quo modo nostrum nec factum est, nec fieri potuit Adami peccatum.
